name: Beth Moreau

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I’m with the independent Work Futures Panel. We have no ties to employers, AI companies, unions or government, and your answers stay confidential. What is a usual day at work?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I’m 43 and manage six people who prepare import documents at a large shipping company. We match container numbers to invoices, check release papers and call the port when a seal number does not agree. I have a bachelor’s degree and have held this manager job for eight years. I know the usual cases well and send the difficult rules to our legal team. I have never used an AI tool; I prefer a signed document and a person at the gate.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: And what is your household situation?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My husband teaches at a primary school, and our children are nine and fifteen. We have a mortgage and around nine months of expenses saved. I earn above the usual manager rate because I cover late arrivals, and there are plenty of logistics jobs near the port. I like the children to see that a promise about work means showing up and checking it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. "Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell my team AI Plateau is another filing shortcut. The container still needs the right seal and the correct paper before it leaves the port.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think my hours and income stay safe. We have nine months saved and two steady wages, so a routine tool does not change our household plans. I would still worry about a late ship and a missing document, as I do now.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’d keep the second clerk check on every changed seal number and call the gate supervisor when the papers disagree. If a sorter arrives, I’d ask our senior clerk to show me its rejected files before I let it touch live releases. We would keep paying a little extra on the mortgage each full-pay month.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel calm about work and money. I do not need a new screen to tell me whether a seal is wrong.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What happened with a seal this month?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The paper listed seal 4187, but the metal seal on the load read 4178. A clerk caught the reversal before a driver queued at the gate. Ten minutes of checking saved a return trip.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why not try the sorter yourself?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I have not used AI before, and our senior clerk knows where document mistakes hide. I would listen to her and watch the rejected pile. I will not sign a release because a screen is neat.

say: **AI Plateau** might speed filing, while people still check container seals.
A release needs the **right paper** before the driver reaches the gate.
think: My **hours and income** seem secure under a small tool change.
Late ships and missing documents remain the **ordinary risk** at work.
do: **Keep** second checks on changed seal numbers in 2026.
**Ask** the senior clerk to show rejected files before using a sorter.
**Continue** small extra mortgage payments in full-pay months.
feel: I feel **calm** about work and bills in this mild picture.
S0.quote: The paper listed seal 4187, but the metal seal on the load read 4178.
fieldNote: Her **nine-month reserve** and two wages make a minor filing aid unthreatening.
She has **never used AI** and relies on the senior clerk’s rejected files before approving a sorter.

steps.text: Keep second clerk checks on changed container seal numbers
Continue extra mortgage payments only in full-pay months

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. "Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say Steady Disruption will write forms, check numbers, plan collection slots and answer routine customers. The company can use it, but it should count wrong releases and pay staff to learn the new process.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately, that is most of my desk. I know the work, but another port office could absorb our team and remove one manager. The cushion gives us time, yet I would not call a lost high-paid post harmless just because other firms have vacancies.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This year I’d ask the port gate manager for a list of wrong releases and compare it with our document record. If the company approves a new checker, I’d attend a paid lesson with the senior clerk and use it only after we have found its errors. If our office shrinks, I’d apply for an advertised gate-operations manager role only if its pay and shifts fit the mortgage and our school week.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about my post, even though we could pay the bills while I looked. A vacant job is not the same as an offer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Which wrong release would you count?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A driver was once sent to collect a refrigerated load with the wrong seal number. The gate stopped it, and our desk corrected the paper before the truck returned. I would count both the saved cargo and the wasted trip.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you accept a night shift at the gate?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Only after my husband and I checked the school week. He teaches early, so one of us needs to be at home when the nine-year-old wakes. I would not take a higher wage that leaves a child alone.

say: **Document automation** should be judged by wrong releases and wasted trips.
The company should pay for **new process training** before staff sign releases.
think: Another port office could absorb our desk and remove **my manager post**.
Nine months saved buys time, but losing **higher pay** would still matter.
do: **Compare** gate release errors with document records this year.
**Attend** approved paid checker instruction with the senior clerk before live use.
**Apply** for advertised gate work only if pay and shifts fit mortgage and school week.
feel: I feel **anxious** about a possible merger despite our savings.
S1.quote: I would not take a higher wage that leaves a child alone.
fieldNote: Her **careful training condition** fits someone who has never used AI and wants errors shown first.
The **gate role** depends on an actual posting and shifts that leave an adult home with the younger child.

steps.text: Compare wrong gate releases against the import document record
Attend paid checker instruction and practise only after senior clerk shows errors
Apply for posted gate role only if pay and shifts cover mortgage and school care

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. "Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell the team AGI by 2028 could prepare and check nearly every import document. We should get written cut dates and make sure a person can stop a wrong release at the gate.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Full thinking AI in 2028 could do my paperwork before capable robots move and inspect loads around 2031. A gate manager also writes reports and plans slots, so that work faces AGI in 2028 too. I expect the document desk to shrink, and my post could be removed. Our reserve buys time but does not replace my wage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Tomorrow I’d request written staffing and severance terms from my director. I’d compare two posted gate jobs with my current pay and apply only if they include real seal checks and shifts my husband and I can cover. If AGI arrives in 2028 and my post ends, I’d accept a confirmed gate offer only if pay after travel covers our mortgage and childcare.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about leaving a job I know. We have room to search, and I will not promise my team that another port will hire us all.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Does a gate job stay safe?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The gate reports and slot planning could change in 2028, and robots around 2031 could change the physical checks. I would ask exactly which decisions the gate manager still makes. A current vacancy is useful, not a life guarantee.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you move the family?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No, not for an advert. The children are in school and my husband teaches nearby. I would try a commute only after a confirmed offer and a calculation of travel costs.

say: **AGI by 2028** needs cut dates and a human stop at the gate.
I would not promise staff a **new port job** without an offer.
think: Paperwork and gate scheduling face **2028 AGI**, before load robots around 2031.
My post could end, though a **nine-month reserve** buys search time.
do: **Request** written staffing and severance terms tomorrow.
**Apply** for posted gate jobs only with real seal checks and family-compatible shifts.
**Accept** a confirmed gate offer only if travel-adjusted pay covers mortgage and childcare.
feel: I feel **anxious** about leaving familiar work, with time to search.
S2.quote: A current vacancy is useful, not a life guarantee.
fieldNote: She sees **gate paperwork** exposed in 2028 and physical checks changing after robots arrive around 2031.
Her **commute** depends on a confirmed offer and travel costs; the family is not moving on an advert.

steps.text: Apply for posted gate jobs only with real seal checks and family-compatible shifts
Accept confirmed gate offer only if pay after travel covers mortgage and childcare

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. "Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say AGI by 2031 gives us five years to learn what a gate manager does when a seal is wrong. I would rather spend a paid day at the port than buy an online badge.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My document desk and gate reports could still change in 2031. Robots that move and inspect loads arrive around 2034, so the physical gate work may last a little longer. I have nearby options but no promise that the right shift will be open when I need it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In January 2027 I’d ask for three paid gate shifts with the gate manager, but take them only if my director covers our document desk and keeps my salary. I’d practise checking a seal against the load record under the manager’s eye. After 2031 I’d apply for a gate vacancy only if its pay after travel covers our mortgage and its shifts fit the family.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about the desk, but the paid shifts would show what I need to learn. I can work hard at a real task; I do not want a course title.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you ask at the gate?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Who can stop the truck and who signs a corrected release. I know the document number, not every step between the yard and the road. I would ask the manager to correct my record before I tried it alone.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if those shifts are unpaid?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would not take them. My husband’s teacher pay does not need to carry the mortgage while I try a possible job. I would ask for paid time or continue my present work.

say: **Five years** allows paid gate shifts before a job change.
I would learn the **seal check** under a manager’s eye.
think: Documents and gate reports face **2031 AGI**, before load robots around 2034.
A suitable **gate shift** may not be open when I need it.
do: **Take** three paid gate shifts from January 2027 only with desk cover and full salary.
**Practise** seal checks under gate-manager review during those paid shifts.
**Apply** after 2031 only if net gate pay covers mortgage and family shifts work.
feel: I feel **anxious** about desk changes, with a paid way to test gate work.
S3.quote: I know the document number, not every step between the yard and the road.
fieldNote: She prefers **three paid shifts** to an online certificate, matching her resistant approach to technology.
The paid shifts need **desk cover** and full salary; a later vacancy needs mortgage pay and family-compatible hours.

steps.text: Take three paid gate shifts only with document-desk cover and full salary
Practise seal checks under gate-manager review during paid shifts
Apply after 2031 only if net gate pay covers mortgage and family shifts work

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. "Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say AGI by 2036 gives employers ten years to show which port jobs actually remain. I would ask for posted wages and shifts before a worker is told to change trades.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: By 2036 our children will be about nineteen and twenty-five. If both wages continue, we may have finished much of the mortgage and kept a strong reserve. My document and gate-report work still faces thinking AI in 2036; robots for physical loads follow around 2039. I do not need to leave this job early just because a card says a date.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’d keep the seal-number second check and our full-pay-month mortgage overpayment. Each spring I’d review real gate-manager vacancies and ask the manager what decisions still need a person. Before 2036 I’d take a paid gate posting only if it protects our income and family rota; after AGI arrives I’d stay only while it has real checks and pays our bills.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel calm about the next few years. Ten years and a strong reserve leave us time to judge real work.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you retire early if the desk ended?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No. At 43 I have years of paid work ahead, and our children may still need help when they start adult life. I would rather learn the gate trade than sit at home spending our savings. I would ask for a real job description.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Could you move later?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: When the children are grown, my husband and I could consider it for an actual offer. We would compare his teaching work and our mortgage first. We do not need to move for an untested post today.

say: A **decade** should bring posted port jobs, wages and shifts.
I would ask for **real gate decisions** before changing work.
think: Two wages could reduce the **mortgage** while keeping a strong reserve.
Documents and gate reports face **2036 AGI**, before load robots around 2039.
do: **Keep** second seal checks and full-pay mortgage overpayments in 2026.
**Review** gate vacancies each spring with the manager’s duty list.
**Take** a paid gate posting only with protected income and family rota; stay after 2036 only if checks still pay bills.
feel: I feel **calm** about near-term work, with time to choose.
S4.quote: I would rather learn the gate trade than sit at home spending our savings.
fieldNote: Her **traditional view** favours paid practical learning and continued work over early retirement.
The **children’s ages** make relocation a later question, always tied to a real offer and teaching work.

steps.text: Keep second checks on changed container seal numbers through 2026
Continue extra mortgage payments only in full-pay months
Review gate vacancies each spring and take only with protected pay and rota
Stay in gate role after 2036 only with paid checks covering household bills

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because the document team could shrink before I have practised gate work. A written cut date, real severance terms and paid shifts at the gate would help. Nine months saved lets me choose an offer, not promise every clerk a new job.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn’t ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Ask the driver who has to turn back when one seal digit is wrong. A form can look complete while the gate refuses the load. Someone needs to check the metal seal before release.

headlineQuote: A form can look complete while the gate refuses the load.
portrait: **Beth, 43**, is an experienced import-document manager leading six clerks at a large shipping company.
Her **high pay**, teacher husband, nine-month reserve and many port jobs support a mortgage and two school-age children.
She has **never used AI** and prefers signed papers, seal checks and advice from an experienced clerk.
She is **calm** under AI Plateau, anxious about a fast desk cut and tests paid gate work under salary conditions.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could shrink her document team before she has tested gate work.
whatWouldHelp: Written **cut dates**, severance terms and paid gate shifts would help her choose.
